senses.definition: (transitive) To present again or anew; to present by means of something standing in the place of; to exhibit the counterpart or image of; to typify.

examples: a landscape can be represented in a picture.
The sculptor represented a horse in bronze.

senses.definition: (transitive) To portray by mimicry or acting; to act the part or character of
examples: It has always been his dream to represent Hamlet on Broadway.

senses.definition: (transitive) To stand or act in the place of; to perform the duties, exercise the rights, or otherwise act on behalf of
examples: He sent his agent to represent himself at the meeting.
As he was too ill to accept the award, his brother represented him at the ceremony.
An attorney's job is to represent his client in court

senses.definition: (politics, transitive) To act as a representative of (a country, state, district etc.)
examples: They chose a member of Congress to represent their district.

senses.definition: (transitive) To portray to another using language; to show; to give one's own impressions and judgement of
examples: He represented that he was investigating for the police department.

senses.definition: (transitive) To give an account of; to describe.
(transitive) To serve as a sign or symbol of.
examples: The @ symbol represents the online world.
A dove is often used to represent peace.

quotes.text: A person climbs a mountain, not only "because it is there," but also because it represents a fundamental and personal challenge.
quotes.reference: 1983, Richard Ellis, The Book of Sharks, Knopf, →ISBN, page 150:

senses.definition: (transitive) To bring a certain sensation of into the mind; to cause to be known, felt, or apprehended; to present.
(transitive) To form or image again in consciousness, as an object of cognition or apprehension (something presentative, which was originally apprehended by direct presentation).
(transitive) To constitute, to make up, to be an example of.

quotes.text: Rounded stone and glass objects with fine radiating scratches on one surface represent the slickstones that were used in garment-making and laundry, to smooth the cloth and to press seams and pleats.
quotes.reference: 2020 January 31, Penelope Walton Rogers, “Textile networks in Viking-age towns of Britain and Ireland”, in Stephen P. Ashby, Søren Sindbæk, editors, Crafts and Social Networks in Viking Towns, →ISBN, page 101:

senses.definition: (sports, transitive) To participate as a team member.
(poker, transitive) To play as if holding (a set of cards); to play as if having made (a hand).
examples: Richard was holding the nuts, but he was trying to represent two-pair to get the other players to bet.

senses.definition: (intransitive, African-American Vernacular) To constitute a good example or symbol of a group of people; to acquit oneself well.

I'm representing for the gangsters all across the world.

senses.definition: (medicine) To present again, for instance for medical attention.
(by extension) To present again, possibly in an altered form.
examples: video game represented as live-action television
